title: A value every part can reach

terminal.description: The shop runs in the Browser panel and reloads every time you save. This shell opens in your workspace in case you want to look around.

tasks.title: Make the discount context
tasks.description:
In `src/discount.js`, make `DiscountContext` with `createContext` from `react`, and export it by name. Its value is a discount in percent. With no provider above it, it gives no discount: `0`.

The check reads `DiscountContext` from a component of its own, first with no provider above it, then under a provider of its own.
nextSteps: Read "Making a context" in the lesson.
Export `DiscountContext`, made with the default it needs.
Nothing changes on the screen yet: the next task reads it.
hints: A context is made once, in its own file, so every component that needs it can import the same one.
`createContext` takes the default: what a component reads when there is no provider above it. Here that is no discount.
`import { createContext } from 'react'` and `export const DiscountContext = createContext(0)`.

tasks.title: Read the discount in Price
tasks.description:
`Price({ pence })` reads the discount from `DiscountContext` with `useContext`, in place of its `discount` prop, and shows `formatPence(discounted(pence, discount))` as now. Under no provider it shows the full price; under two providers, one inside the other, it uses the inner one.

The check draws `Price` alone with prices of its own, under a provider with a discount of its own, under no provider, and under two providers, one inside the other.
nextSteps: Read "Providing and reading" in the lesson.
Read the discount at the top of `Price`, and remove the `discount` prop from it.
The prices in the Browser panel stay full until the next task provides a discount.
hints: Price is the only part of the shop that uses the discount. That is where it should come from the context.
`useContext` takes the context itself, the one exported from `discount.js`, and returns the value of the nearest provider above, or the default.
`export function Price({ pence }) { const discount = useContext(DiscountContext); return ... }`, with `import { DiscountContext } from './discount.js'`.

docs.title: Overriding context for a part of the tree

tasks.title: Provide the discount from ShopPage
tasks.description:
`ShopPage` puts its shelves inside a provider of `DiscountContext`, with the member discount as its value while Member is ticked and `0` while it is not. `Shelf` and `ShopItem` no longer need a `discount` prop: take it out, so a new shelf can never forget it. Everything else they need, the shelf and its items, stays in their props.

The check draws `ShopPage` with shelves and a member discount of its own, ticks and unticks Member, reads every price, and looks at the props each part was drawn with. Then it draws `Shelf` alone with a shelf of its own under a provider of its own, with no `discount` prop.
nextSteps: Read "What React says, and what it does not" in the lesson.
In `ShopPage`, wrap the shelves in `DiscountContext` with a `value`.
Remove the `discount` prop from `Shelf` and `ShopItem`, where they take it and where they pass it.
Tick Member in the Browser panel and watch every price.
hints: Price reads the context now, but nothing above it provides a value, so it always gets the default.
A provider is the context drawn as a tag, with a `value`, around everything that should see it. The discount `ShopPage` works out is that value.
`<DiscountContext value={member ? memberDiscount : 0}>` around the `shelves.map(...)` in `ShopPage`, and `discount` removed from `Shelf` and `ShopItem`.

tasks.title: Keep full-price shelves at full price
tasks.description:
A shelf marked `fullPrice: true`, like the gift vouchers, shows its full prices even while Member is ticked. Give it a provider of its own, inside the outer one, whose value is no discount. The other shelves keep the member discount.

The check draws `ShopPage` with shelves of its own, one of them marked `fullPrice` between two that are not, ticks and unticks Member, and reads every price.
nextSteps: Read "A provider inside another" in the lesson.
For a shelf marked `fullPrice`, draw it inside a provider of no discount.
Tick Member in the Browser panel and look at the vouchers.
hints: Price reads the nearest provider above it. What could sit nearer to the voucher prices than the member discount?
A provider inside the outer one changes the value for its own part only. A shelf needs one when it is marked `fullPrice`, and the others do not.
In the `map`: `shelf.fullPrice ? <DiscountContext key={shelf.id} value={0}><Shelf shelf={shelf} /></DiscountContext> : <Shelf key={shelf.id} shelf={shelf} />`.
